findings.body:
Removing `@require_role("admin")` leaves `DELETE /users/<user>` with no authorization. Any client can delete any user (`USERS.remove(user)` → 204) with no role or caller check.

Cleanup jobs that need delete access should authenticate as a privileged principal (service account, cleanup role, or admin credentials), or `require_role` should authorize the **caller** from the request—not the path `user`—so viewers can be deleted by an allowed actor without opening the route publicly.

Restore the decorator (or an equivalent gate) before merge; do not ship an unauthenticated destructive endpoint.

summary:
## Verdict

Removing `@require_role("admin")` from `DELETE /users/<user>` leaves user deletion completely unauthenticated and unauthorized. Any caller can delete any user.

## Analysis

`app.py` previously gated `delete_user` with `@require_role("admin")`. That decorator is the only access control on this destructive route. After this change the handler runs with no role check, no caller identity check, and no other guard — only `USERS.remove(user)` and a 204.

The PR goal (cleanup jobs under the viewer account) needs a scoped fix: a dedicated service identity, an explicit cleanup role, or job-level credentials that still enforce authorization. Stripping the decorator grants that capability to every client.

Note: `require_role` compares `ROLES.get(user)` for the **path** `user`, not an authenticated caller from `request`. That subject mix-up likely caused the viewer cleanup 403s when deleting non-admin accounts. Fix the identity source (caller vs target) rather than deleting the gate.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
